confirm.title: Librescoot-BLE-Client
confirm.description: Set up the discovered LibreScoot device "{name}"? Its entities are detected automatically. Relay settings (host, port, GitHub token) are in the Librescoot – Relay entry; the update channel is in this entry's options.

user.title: Librescoot-BLE-Client
user.description: What do you want to add?

menu_options.new_esp: Set up a new ESP (creates its ESPHome configuration)
menu_options.adopt: Adopt an ESPHome configuration I wrote myself (check it, link it)
menu_options.esp: Add an ESP that is already set up in ESPHome

esp.title: Librescoot-BLE-Client
esp.description: Enter the ESPHome node name of your librescoot_ble_client device (used for the pairing action). Everything else is auto-detected; tune it later in the options.

wiz_resume.title: Unfinished ESP setup
wiz_resume.description: There is an unfinished setup for **{node}** (step {step} of {count}, saved {age} ago).

wiz_chip.title: New ESP — 1/6 Chip
wiz_chip.description:
Which board is it? Look at the module label: the number after **R** is the PSRAM size (e.g. N16R8 = 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM). Boards without PSRAM get firmware through Home Assistant.

Or let the browser read it: plug the ESP into this computer and open {usb_link} — it opens in a new tab and needs Chrome or Edge with Home Assistant over HTTPS. Then come back to this tab and choose "fetch its result".

wiz_scooter.title: New ESP — 2/6 Scooter
wiz_scooter.description: Home Assistant hears {count} scooter(s) nearby. Pick one, type its Bluetooth address, or set it later.

data.mac: Bluetooth address (only for "Enter the scooter's Bluetooth address")

wiz_name.title: New ESP — 3/6 Name
wiz_name.description: The node name becomes the ESP's network name and the file name in your ESPHome folder: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 31 characters.

wiz_wifi.title: New ESP — 4/6 WiFi
wiz_wifi.description: Reuse WiFi secrets from your ESPHome secrets.yaml, or enter a network. A new password is written to secrets.yaml only and is not kept by Home Assistant.

data.use_token: Use the GitHub token from secrets.yaml
data.github_token: GitHub token (optional; raises GitHub's request limit)

wiz_write.title: New ESP — 6/6 Create
wiz_write.description: Create **{file}** for **{node}** ({chip}, scooter {scooter}) from the example configuration on GitHub, and add its secrets to `esphome/secrets.yaml` (nothing there is changed or removed). {where} {error}

wiz_download.title: New ESP — download
wiz_download.description:
Nothing was written on this Home Assistant. Download both files (links stay valid for 30 minutes):

- {yaml_link} — put it next to your other ESPHome configurations
- {secrets_link} — **append** these lines to your ESPHome `secrets.yaml`, do not replace the file

Or copy the secret lines from here:
```yaml
{secrets}
```
Submit to add the ESP to the integration.

adopt.title: Adopt an ESPHome configuration
adopt.description: These configurations in your ESPHome folder use the librescoot_ble_client component. Pick one; it is checked first and only changed where you agree.

abort.wizard_done_existing: The configuration was created; this ESP was already added to the integration.
abort.adopt_none: No configuration in your ESPHome folder uses the librescoot_ble_client component.

error.invalid_node: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 31 characters, starting with a letter or digit.
error.node_exists: An ESPHome configuration or device with this name already exists.
error.wifi_missing: Enter the network name and the password.
error.github_unreachable: Could not fetch the example configuration from GitHub. Check the internet connection and try again.
error.adopt_no_name: This file's node name could not be read (esphome: name:).
error.adopt_linked: This ESP is already added to the integration.
error.adopt_psram_both: Choose only one of the two PSRAM changes.
error.adopt_key_exists: secrets.yaml already has a key with the name this change would use; move the API key by hand.

create_entry.wizard_done:
Created **esphome/{node}.yaml**. Next: open **ESPHome Device Builder**, select **{node}**, choose **Install → Plug into this computer** and connect the ESP by USB. When Home Assistant then reports the new ESPHome device, enter this encryption key:

`{key}`{mac_note}
create_entry.adopt_done: Linked **{node}** ({file}). {changed} Install it again from the ESPHome Device Builder if anything was changed.

data.ota_source: OTA byte source (set on the ESP)
data.alarm_code: Alarm panel code (optional, digits; empty = no code)
data.alarm_disarm_disables: Disarming also disables the scooter alarm

scooter.title: This ESP’s scooter
scooter.description: {mac} — {status}. “Enter passkey (pair)” only appears when the scooter is actually asking for one.

manual.title: Enter a scooter MAC
manual.description: Type the scooter's BLE MAC (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF). Put it into the ESPHome YAML's `mac_address:` and reflash for the ESP to use it.

scan_result.title: Pick your scooter
scan_result.description: Found {count} scooter(s). Ones this ESP hears come first, strongest signal first — place the ESP on the scooter you mean and take the top one. **new** = no ESP uses it yet; **connected to …** = another ESP holds it (a connected scooter does not advertise, so only that ESP knows it); **paired with …** = another ESP's scooter that is not connected right now.

pair.title: Enter the pairing passkey
pair.description: The scooter dashboard shows a 6-digit passkey. Enter it here to finish bonding the ESP with the scooter.

unbind.title: Remove bond?
unbind.description: Remove this ESP's bond to {mac}? The ESP forgets the scooter and re-pairs (you'll enter the passkey again) on the next connect. Your phone pairing is not affected. Submit to confirm.

mac_note.title: Use this scooter
mac_note.description: The ESP takes its scooter from its ESPHome configuration (`mac_address:`). Let the integration write **{mac}** there — into secrets.yaml when the YAML reads it from a secret, else into the YAML (the previous file is kept as .bak) — and then install the ESP again. Untick to only remember it here and change the YAML yourself. {error}

data.write: Write the scooter address into the ESP's configuration

relay.title: Librescoot – Relay
relay.description: Home-Assistant-wide settings. The ESPs fetch firmware, release lists and delta checks from this relay (when their OTA Source is "HA relay"). Changing host or port re-points every ESP automatically.

data.ha_host: Host/IP the ESPs use to reach the relay
data.github_token: GitHub token (optional, raises the rate limit)

mac_done.title: Scooter written
mac_done.description:
{changed}

Now install **{node}** again from the ESPHome Device Builder (*Install → Wirelessly*). Then pair it when the scooter shows a code.

progress.scanning: Scanning for scooters… the ESP is briefly switched to scan mode (~18 s), then restored.

error.no_scooter_found: No scooter adverts seen. Make sure the scooter is nearby and awake, then Scan again.

start.title: Pair the scooter ({node})

menu_options.pair: Start pairing (the scooter will show a code)

pair.title: Enter the passkey
pair.description:
Pairing was started on the ESP — the scooter dashboard shows a 6-digit passkey (signal: {rssi}).

It can take about 10–15 seconds for the code to appear after the scooter wakes — please wait for it. Then enter it here to finish bonding.

failed.title: Pairing didn't complete
failed.description: No connection was established for {node} — the code may have been wrong or the scooter went out of range ({rssi}). Submit to try again.

progress.verifying: Finishing pairing… waiting for the encrypted connection to the scooter to come up.

confirm.title: Restart the scooter
confirm.description: A firmware update for {node} has finished installing but the scooter has been waiting for the reboot that applies it for over 20 minutes. Submit to restart the scooter now and finish the update.

confirm.title: Add the Librescoot – Relay again
confirm.description: The Librescoot – Relay entry was removed. Without it the ESPs in "HA relay" mode get no firmware, no release list and no delta checks. Submit to add it again with default settings (port 8127). The ESPs' URLs stay valid unless you had changed host or port.

esp_not_linked.title: ESP not found for {title}
esp_not_linked.description:
The Librescoot entry **{title}** cannot find its ESPHome device (node `{node}`, MAC `{mac}`). Without it there is no pairing Repair, no relay URL and no update steering.

Fix: add the ESP in the ESPHome integration, or remove this entry and add it again with the ESP's exact node name.

relay_url_mismatch.title: {title} uses a different relay URL
relay_url_mismatch.description:
The ESP of **{title}** is in "HA relay" mode but uses
`{esp_url}`
instead of the relay's
`{want_url}`.

The integration writes the relay URL into the ESP as soon as the ESP is connected to Home Assistant; this message then disappears by itself. If it stays while the ESP is online, check that its YAML does not fix the OTA Source URL and that host/port in the Librescoot – Relay entry are reachable from the ESP.

confirm.title: Point the ESP at the relay
confirm.description:
The ESP is in "HA relay" mode but downloads from
`{esp_url}`
instead of the relay's
`{want_url}`.

Submit to write the relay URL into the ESP now, over its ESPHome connection (it keeps it across restarts).

error.url_not_taken: The ESP did not accept the URL. Check that its OTA Source select is "HA relay" and that its YAML does not fix the URL.
error.esp_unreachable: The ESP is not connected to Home Assistant right now. Try again when it is online.

abort.esp_not_loaded: This ESP's integration entry is not loaded.

no_scooter.title: {title} has no scooter set
no_scooter.description: The ESP **{node}** does not know which scooter to connect to (its scooter MAC is empty). Open this repair while the ESP is online to scan for scooters and set one.

scan.title: Looking for scooters
scan.description: The ESP scans for about 20 seconds.

pick.title: Pick the scooter
pick.description: Found {count} scooter(s). Ones this ESP hears come first, strongest signal first — place the ESP on the scooter you mean and take the top one. **new** = no ESP uses it yet; **connected to …** = another ESP holds it (a connected scooter does not advertise, so only that ESP knows it); **paired with …** = another ESP's scooter that is not connected right now.

done.title: Scooter set
done.description:
{changed}

Now install **{node}** again from the ESPHome Device Builder (*Install → Wirelessly*). After the install the ESP connects to the scooter; pair it when the scooter shows a code.

init.title: Set a scooter for {node}
init.description: How do you want to pick the scooter?

menu_options.scan: Scan with this ESP (about 20 seconds; place the ESP on or next to the scooter)
menu_options.known: Choose from the scooters already known (Home Assistant's Bluetooth and your other ESPs)

manual.title: Enter the scooter's address
manual.description: The Bluetooth address of the scooter, e.g. from the scooter's settings or another ESP's **BLE Scooter nRF MAC**.

progress.scanning: The ESP scans for scooters (about 20 seconds)…

error.none_known: No scooter known yet. Scan with this ESP, or go back and enter the address.

abort.esp_not_loaded: This ESP's integration entry is not loaded.

passkey_reply.name: Send passkey
passkey_reply.description: Forward the 6-digit passkey shown on the scooter dashboard to the ESPHome component during pairing.

pin.name: PIN
pin.description: The 6-digit passkey shown on the scooter dashboard.

node.name: Node
node.description: ESPHome node name — only needed if more than one device is configured.

update.name: Prepare / install firmware
update.description: Point the ESP's OTA source at Home Assistant's byte listener and optionally arm the install gate and start the install.

install.name: Install
install.description: On = arm the gate and install; off = only prepare (stage-only).

node.name: Node
node.description: ESPHome node name — only needed if more than one device is configured.

reboot_scooter.name: Restart scooter
reboot_scooter.description: Restart the scooter to apply a firmware update that finished installing but is stuck waiting for its reboot.

node.name: Node
node.description: ESPHome node name — only needed if more than one device is configured.
